Minimal clinically important difference (MCID) thresholds

Source: R/thresholds-mcid.R
mcid_thresholds.Rd

Define the boundaries of a "trivial" zone around the null, flanked by a "benefit" zone and a "harm" zone, for use with geom_mcid_zones().

Usage

mcid_thresholds(
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  direction = c("higher_better", "lower_better"),
  source = NULL,
  provisional = FALSE,
  mcid = NULL
)

Arguments

lower, upper

Thresholds on the difference scale: lower < 0 < upper. Each is a number or a length-2 range.

direction

Whether higher ("higher_better") or lower ("lower_better") values of the outcome are desirable.

source

Optional citation for the thresholds, shown in the legend title.

provisional

TRUE when the thresholds are not patient-derived (e.g. distribution-based, see mcid_distribution()). The legend title then says so.

mcid

Symmetric shorthand: a positive number (or length-2 positive range) used for both sides. Cannot be combined with lower/upper.

Value

An object of class mcid_thresholds.

Details

lower and upper are positions on the difference scale, relative to the null: lower must be negative and upper positive. Which of them is the improvement threshold depends on direction:

  • "higher_better": differences above upper are benefit, below lower are harm (deterioration).

  • "lower_better": differences below lower are benefit, above upper are harm.

The two thresholds need not be equal in size (asymmetric MCIDs are common, for example when deterioration is felt at a smaller change than improvement). Each may be a single value or a length-2 range, which expresses uncertainty about where the threshold lies (for example, two anchor-based studies that disagree). geom_mcid_zones() draws a range as a gradual transition rather than a line.

A single positive value mcid = x is shorthand for lower = -x, upper = x. A length-2 positive mcid gives a symmetric range.

References

Jaeschke R, Singer J, Guyatt GH (1989). Measurement of health status: ascertaining the minimal clinically important difference. Controlled Clinical Trials 10(4):407-415. doi:10.1016/0197-2456(89)90005-6

McGlothlin AE, Lewis RJ (2014). Minimal clinically important difference: defining what really matters to patients. JAMA 312(13):1342-1343.

See also

mcid_distribution(), geom_mcid_zones()

Examples

# Symmetric: +/- 10 points
mcid_thresholds(mcid = 10)
#> <mcid_thresholds> (higher_better)
#> harm: difference < -10
#> trivial: between -10 and 10
#> benefit: difference > 10

# Asymmetric, with an uncertain improvement threshold
mcid_thresholds(lower = -5, upper = c(8, 12),
                source = "Anchor-based (two studies)")
#> <mcid_thresholds> (higher_better)
#> harm: difference < -5
#> trivial: between -5 and [8, 12]
#> benefit: difference > [8, 12]
#> Source: Anchor-based (two studies)

# Pain score: lower is better
mcid_thresholds(lower = -1.5, upper = 1, direction = "lower_better")
#> <mcid_thresholds> (lower_better)
#> benefit: difference < -1.5
#> trivial: between -1.5 and 1
#> harm: difference > 1
